items.title: Sal Gutierrez Interview, 1970-01-15
items.q: I tell you one thing about, I got to say about, about Armand Hug. He was always a good piano player for him.

ctx.x: Yeah, he told me that. You're on the fourth rail now. Heavens to Betsy. Yeah, I didn't know. You were telling me about Gordon Kirst before we forget it. He had the band. Yeah, yeah, see the fart there, they got help that the IJ Kirst couldn't play nothing. And Gordon was in the band, see, piano player. So they put Gordon with the baton leading the band.

So naturally, Steve got to play. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. So naturally, Steve got on me in the band to play piano. They all hung up to play piano in the band, not the Blue Room, see. I was the first band in the Blue Room, before I started going to name bands, you know, name bands. The same thing happened at the Club Forest when they had the bands out there, Juice Bidoux and Lou Yandies and bands and bands and bands and they…
What was Eddie Miller playing then? Tennis.

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: I was thinking once, somebody like Sal Gutierrez... showed me a picture once. ... Probably so. Yeah. I did.

ctx.x: Maybe, but, you know, it isn't just the music that interests me. It's also the people and the way the people like music and, you know, what music did for them. And I was thinking once, somebody like Sal Gutierrez, one of those people from up around Coliseum Square showed me a picture once. I think you were playing baseball. Would it have been?
